The screen shows one list to every player, so no line is gated any more: every line that was gated on a badge carries gate_dropped with its old gate. Until 2026-10-06 the keeper was a Cobblemon dialogue NPC with badge-gated options and a checked purchase function (superseded_dialogue_purchase)

income_basis.source: measured from data: the trainer files tools/route_trainers.files() emits (the pack the game reads; Challenge = tools/challenge_mode.py's <id>_challenge copies) under CobbleDollars' battleVictory payout
income_basis.formula: per battle won against an NPC, S = the losing team's level sum: B = max(1, int(5*S*sum(L/50))) = S^2/10; amount = B + nextBetween(B/2, 2B); credit = floor(amount * 1.25). Expected credit = 1.25 * 2.25 * S^2/10 = 0.28125*S^2 (a uniform draw on [B/2, 2B] has mean 1.25B, so E[amount] = 2.25B)
income_basis.formula_source: docs/research/notes/paid-services-and-npc-payouts.md B2 (CobbleDollars battleVictory bytecode 370-567, VERIFIED there; the uniform inclusive draw is ASSUMED there); cobbleDollarsIncomeMultiplier from modpack/config/cobbledollars/common.json
income_basis.unverified: no payout has been read back in game against this model. The two measured payouts ($732, $600, docs/research/INCOME_MEASUREMENT.md) were against UPSTREAM kanto_brock at multiplier 0.5, not our roster (ECONOMY_OVERHAUL.md P1)
income_basis.excluded: wild battles (CobbleDollars pays them under the same formula while earnCobbleDollarsFromWildPokemon is true: owner question 1, ECONOMY_OVERHAUL.md P2; every figure here assumes they pay nothing); Heaven's Arena; rematches; Cobbleverse's roaming trainers and donor-template trainers; the Compact HQ tower (post_badge_8, not in any badge)

income_gate.decision: the owner, 2026-10-09 (docs/STATE.md 'The owner's decisions of 2026-10-09' (1)): 'TMs AT COUNTERS: price them above the income gate. A TM costing less than a player earns before badge 1 is free, and TMs are permanent unlocks. Hold the 41 lines until they clear that bar.' A counter is a merchant and cannot gate a line per player (decision counters_are_merchants), and Fossick and Northlight are ungated off-path towns (data/towns.json gates []), so the price is the gate
income_gate.criterion: a counter line carrying price_rule 'income_gate' declares gate_badge B (1-8) and gate_why. Its unit price is the smallest multiple of round_to STRICTLY above income_basis.cumulative_by_badge[B]: a player holding B-1 badges earns leg B while holding them, so the most such a player can have is cumulative_by_badge[B] before any spending (the same INCOME GATE as data/traders.json stock_policy.mart.early_reach_pricing). An exchange line (exchange_for) keeps its material and takes the smallest whole count of it whose bank value clears the same bar; its price is exactly count x the bank's price (data/bank.json exchanges.shape), so round_to does not apply

gate_badges.tm: a leader's TM (tmcraft:tm_<move> in a first_win_rewards one_of, data/progression.json) gates on the badge its leader gives, the lowest where two leaders offer it (Fire Blast: Blaine, 7). The audit checks gate_badge against progression.json

gate_badges.sachet: 2: Spritzee to Aromatisse is a trade evolution holding the Sachet with no level requirement (data/cobblemon/species/generation6/spritzee.json in Cobblemon-fabric-1.8.0+1.21.1.jar, read 2026-10-09), so the Sachet works the day a Spritzee is caught: Spritzee is tier 3 (data/spawns.json surface.fungal_north.spritzee), and tier N is the leg on the way to gym N (docs/mechanics/ENCOUNTER_DESIGN.md), i.e. holding 2 badges

income_gate.income_is: COMPUTED from data, not verified in game (income_basis.generated_by tools/income_model.py: the emitted Normal rosters under CobbleDollars' battleVictory payout, wild battles excluded). A Challenge player earns more (income_basis.challenge) and buys earlier. A player who earns faster than the model buys earlier: the gate is only as good as the income model
income_gate.held: a counter's held_stock lists lines this rule prices but no merchant sells, each with held.reason and held.why. Reason ball_floor: tools/bank.py exchange_problems needs the Master Ball exchange (northlight_station master_ball, 30 netherite ingots = $27,000) to cost MORE than the dearest non-exchange line on any shelf, so a stocked income-gate line must cost less than the cheapest ball exchange; the audit names a held line the day it would clear that floor. Releasing them needs the owner: raise the Master Ball above the dearest TM, or change the ball floor (tools/bank.py exchange_floors reads 'the dearest non-exchange line on any shelf'; not this unit's tool), or keep them held

curve_scale.status: built as data 2026-10-10 (unit CURVEPRICE); applied by tools/markets.py (curve_prices; `prices --write` writes the result into this file, `audit` refuses a line whose price is not the rule's). NOT bought in game
curve_scale.rule: docs/mechanics/ECONOMY_OVERHAUL.md section 7 R2: every badge's (critical-path convenience lines + curve_rule's fight allowance) / (trainer income + produce allowance + one gathering hour a leg) stays in the band. Power lines are not on the curve and this rule never prices them (their price is price_policies.income_gate's)
curve_scale.band_source: PROGRESSION_LADDER.md 0.3 'cumulative spend stays near 0.65-0.70 of cumulative income at every badge', kept by R2 ('The band stays')
curve_scale.criterion: a critical-path convenience line (every critical counter's, a critical stall's gated ones) carries price_rule 'curve_scale' and list_price. Leg by leg (the hometown's badge 0 shelf is spent in leg 1), one scale for every line of that leg: (the band's midpoint x what the road has earned by that badge - the fight allowance by then - what the earlier legs cost at their written prices) / the leg's list shelf, a pick-one group counted at its dearest. Each price is list_price x its leg's scale rounded to the nearest multiple of round_to x count, and never below one such multiple. A stretch line (decision B7) takes the scale of its affordable_by leg, the leg it is meant to be bought in
curve_scale.list_price: each line's relative worth: the price it carried under PROGRESSION_LADDER rev 2 / TIERED_GOODS before R2 (2026-10-10). The rule never changes it; a re-pricing of one item against another edits list_price, never price
curve_scale.why_scale_not_fewer_lines: badge 1 is over the band at its list prices (1.37). ECONOMY_OVERHAUL 1.2-1.3: the early slope 'comes from S^2, not from any one price', and the design's answer is that early convenience is paid by the farm and mine on top of fights; R2 now counts exactly one gathering hour and the produce allowance, so the early shelf is priced down to what those plus trainer income pay, rather than dropping or moving lines TIERED_GOODS placed. Late legs scale up: 1.3's 'the late surplus is soaked by re-pricing the late convenience strand up to the curve (U5)'
curve_scale.off_path: off-path counters (Fossick, Northlight, Sunset Harbour) are not on the curve and keep hand prices; this rule does not reach them

stalls_basis.why_this_pattern: a stall is a keeper on tools/markets.py's machinery (a dialogue menu and the purchase function whose charge macro EXP-042 proved), not a data/traders.json shopkeeper: a traders.json trader sells its BCA template's own trade list, filtered, so it cannot be told to sell a fishing town's rods or a stationer's paper without an authored CobbleMerchantShop, and that path (the Exchange's) is proof P-7, not run; it is also generated from the installed template, so it cannot be built or tested without a server. The keeper pattern can say exactly what each stall sells, gate a line if one ever needs it, and is placed by R17M with the counters
stalls_basis.budget: every line is an ungated `provision` (vanilla food, tools, rope, paper, fuel): not a rung on the ladder, so not counted by the curve, which stays the counters' (markets.py priced: a gated stall line on the critical path WOULD count). The money they take comes out of the 30-35% the curve leaves for the Mart, ferries, stones and the blackout (income_basis.target_source); each is something a player can also gather or craft, so it is a convenience bought with spare money, never a gate
stalls_basis.prices: above 2.5x data's bank sell-back for every food line (bank.json pays 5-20 for vanilla food; PROGRESSION_LADDER 0.5's multiplier reading), and set against the Mart's own scale (Poke Ball 200, Potion 200): a meal or a bundle of fuel for about one ball, a tool or instrument for two to five

stall_merchant.keeper: every sited stall's AND every sited counter's keeper (since 2026-10-06, decision counters_are_merchants) is a CobbleDollars merchant at its seat (the squares' contract keeper_at, else the record's at/yaw), named keeper.name, NoAI, PersistenceRequired, Invulnerable, Silent, turned to the seat's yaw, tagged cobblers_stall and cobblers_stall_<id> (stall and counter ids never repeat across the two lists); keeper.greeting is not shown (the merchant's screen has none) and is kept for the record
stall_merchant.offers: one CobbleMerchantShop category per stall or counter, named by its `category` (its theme in words); one offer per stock line, Item {count: 1, id: item}, Price the line's UNIT price as a string (price / count; a line whose price does not divide by its count is refused). The merchant screen sells singly with a quantity selector, and every offer in every BCA template and in the staging probe is count 1: what the screen does with Item.count above 1 is not verified (research note, Unknown), so 16 torches for $160 is offered as Torch at $10, sixteen for $160
stall_merchant.money: CobbleDollars' own screen takes the price from the buyer's balance; tools/markets.py emits no purchase function, dialogue or NPC class for any merchant, so nothing charges twice
stall_merchant.replaces: the Cobblemon dialogue keepers R17M placed with spawnnpcat (cobblers:npc_stall_<id> until 2026-10-04, cobblers:npc_market_<id> until 2026-10-06), which carry no tag: each town's merchant place step first runs <town>_clear, which kills every cobblemon:npc within remove_radius of each of the town's merchant seats (the old keeper stood on that seat, or one block behind it on a stall's table before the tents moved the keeper to the open front), then summons; every other placed NPC stands 3.5+ away (NPC_CLEAR). decisions.decision: no counter or stall sells an item that data/arena_fights.json prizes.items gives. Applied 2026-10-09 (design unit U5): holdfast's bottle_cap_gold (obc:bottle_cap_gold, $6,000) moved to the counter's superseded_stock. decisions.what_it_costs: a badge-8 player has no repeatable Gold Bottle Cap: the arena's five cap prizes are once per player, plus one quest reward and one cache

decisions.asked: 2026-10-04 (as gated_counters_stay_dialogue: should the badge-gated counters also become CobbleDollars merchants? default taken: no)
decisions.owner: the owner, after playing: 'need the steve traders gone. the button list for purchases is bad, should be the villagers with ui only'
decisions.decision: yes: every counter is a CobbleDollars merchant at its seat, yaw and name, built as a stall's (stall_merchant). The merchant screen shows one list to every player, so the 53 badge-gated counter lines lose their gates; each keeps its old gate in gate_dropped. The counters' badge still places them on the curve and the backpack ladder (a counter's badge is its town's), but a line is now buyable by anyone who reaches the counter, one badge earlier on the critical path than the ladder's rung
decisions.what_it_costs: per-player stock (MARKET_GATING.md's option 7) is gone from the markets: a player who reaches a town before its gym can buy its shelf. No verified per-player merchant mechanism exists (docs/research/notes/cobbleverse-merchants.md section 4: CobbleDollars 2.0.0+Beta-6's `/cm open shop <id>` is not installed and not tested)
